**Format:** Lecture + strategy exercise | **Links to instructor's own research**

## Topics covered
- Collaborative filtering — intuition and mechanics, without heavy linear algebra
- Content-based vs hybrid recommenders: which fits which business context
- Business KPIs for recommenders: CTR, conversion rate, average basket size
- The relevance vs diversity vs profit triangle — real trade-offs, no perfect answer
- Filter bubbles as both an ethical risk and a business risk (user trust erosion)
- When NOT to recommend: over-recommendation, cannibalisation, and recommendation fatigue

## Strategy exercise
Three fictional retailers, each with different goals and constraints. Students must:
1. Select and justify the right recommender strategy for each retailer
2. Explain the trade-offs they are accepting (e.g. margin vs relevance)
3. Define the KPIs they would use to measure success post-deployment

**Instructor link:** The instructor brings their own recommender research as a live case. Students critique real design choices — this builds critical thinking and shows the gap between academic and production systems.

## Deliverable
- Recommender strategy brief (one page per retailer)
- KPI definition document
